blocks.text: In 1 Samuel 18:10-12, the book attributes the harmful spirit affecting Saul to the LORD and also says that the LORD had departed from Saul. The language should not be reduced to a single medical, psychological, spiritual, or theological diagnosis; the passage itself presents the experience in its own terms.

The David and Goliath account exists in a substantially shorter ancient Greek form and a longer Masoretic form. How those forms are related remains disputed, so reconstructions of the literary relationship should be held cautiously.

sections.title: A textual question about the preceding account
